categories.label: Rent or mortgage
categories.hint: What you pay. If Housing Benefit goes straight to your landlord, enter only what is left for you to pay, and do not enter that benefit as income.

categories.label: Council Tax
categories.hint: The bill after any Council Tax Reduction or discount.

categories.label: Gas, electricity and other fuel
categories.hint: The bill after any discount, such as the Warm Home Discount.

categories.label: Other housing costs
categories.hint: For example repairs, maintenance and service charges.

categories.label: Food and non-alcoholic drinks
categories.hint: Includes eating out and takeaways, as the example budgets do.

categories.label: Household goods
categories.hint: Includes a weekly share of things replaced now and then, such as a cooker or a bed.

categories.label: Household services
categories.hint: For example phone, internet and postage.

categories.label: Personal goods and services
categories.hint: For example toiletries, hairdressing, prescriptions, dental and eye care.

categories.label: Other travel
categories.hint: For example buses, trains and taxis.

categories.label: Social and cultural activities
categories.hint: For example TV licence, hobbies, gifts and holidays. Eating out goes under food, as in the example budgets.

categories.label: Disability and care costs
categories.hint: No example budget includes these. Enter your own.

income.label: Benefits you actually receive
income.hint: For example Pension Credit, Attendance Allowance or Housing Benefit paid to you. Do not enter a benefit you have not claimed.

presets.label: Single pensioner, renting privately: Minimum Income Standard 2026
presets.geography: United Kingdom, urban areas outside London
presets.housing: One-bedroom flat rented privately at the lower quartile of rents in the East Midlands. The rent is an indication only.
presets.exclusions: No extra costs of disability or care. No car. Assumes relatively good health. No tax: the figures are spending, so the income needed is higher if tax is due.
presets.note: Food includes some money for eating out and takeaways, as the source says.

presets.label: One person, social renter: Retirement Living Standard, minimum
presets.table_reference: Table 3 (2025 column) and Table 5. The rent is the total with social rent in Table 5, less the total with no rent.
presets.geography: United Kingdom, urban areas outside London
presets.housing: Social rent, East Midlands average. The rent is an indication only and takes no account of Housing Benefit.
presets.exclusions: No social care, no dependants, no pets. No tax: the figures are spending after tax, so the income needed is higher if tax is due.
presets.note: This budget is the Minimum Income Standard pensioner budget for 2025. It is a year older than the 2026 budgets and uses an earlier basket. The source counts a year as 365 days. This tool counts 52 weeks, so its yearly total is about 0.3% lower than the yearly figure the source publishes. Food includes meals out and takeaways: the source counts food bought outside the home in its food line.
